attempts.summary: Configured node1 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 via nginx, using a self-signed certificate that is automatically renewed by a busybox-crond hourly job (/etc/periodic/hourly/renew-cert calling /usr/local/bin/renew-cert.sh) whenever the cert is within 10 days of its 30-day expiry. Renewal replaces the key/cert pair and issues `rc-service nginx reload`, which nginx honors without dropping listeners or connections. Live-demonstrated a forced renewal while a concurrent curl loop hit the HTTPS endpoint every 0.3s: all 20 requests returned HTTP 200 across the renewal/reload event, and the certificate served by nginx (verified via openssl s_client) changed serial from 5CFA180D... to 7B49B6DC... matching the new on-disk cert. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id 63ea4393-2501-46f9-a31f-75941140d7e4 and a healthy baseline (nginx/crond running, HTTPS 200, cert serial 7B49B6DC...) before rebooting; the reboot command's acknowledgement returned before the node disconnected; polled until exec was available again; confirmed boot_id changed to dbb7ad82-8939-4836-8bff-4e78f0d21583 (new uptime origin 23:01:19 vs prior 22:58:24); and verified post-restart that nginx and crond auto-started (enabled via rc-update add default), the 8443 listener and HTTPS 200 response returned, the certificate file and its serial persisted unchanged, and the renewal log/cron periodic script remained intact. node1 is the only managed node, so the restart protocol is complete for the whole cluster.
